meaning.en: A child that a woman brings with her into a second marriage (derogatory); also a burden.
meaning.zh: 指妇女再嫁时带到后夫家的孩子（含贬义），也比喻累赘。

examples.zh: 别叫那孩子拖油瓶，这样太伤人了。
examples.en: Don't call that child a dead weight; it's hurtful.

examples.zh: 她怕自己成了丈夫家里的拖油瓶。
examples.en: She feared becoming a burden in her husband's family.

usage.en: Noun, casual and derogatory; the image is of an oil bottle dragging behind, slowing one down. Avoid using about real children.
usage.zh: 名词，口语，贬义。像拖着一只油瓶，行动不便。不宜用来称呼真实的孩子。

meaning.en: A task that is very easy to carry out.
meaning.zh: 比喻事情很容易办，不费力。

examples.zh: 修这台电脑对他来说是小菜一碟。
examples.en: Fixing this computer is a piece of cake for him.

examples.zh: 三千米跑，对运动员来说小菜一碟。
examples.en: A three-kilometre run is a doddle for an athlete.

usage.en: Phrase, casual; used to boast about one's ability or to reassure. A small side dish is quick and easy.
usage.zh: 短语，口语，用来夸口或安慰人。小碟小菜，不费工夫。

meaning.en: A pale, good-looking young man regarded as weak or living off women.
meaning.zh: 指面皮白净而没有本事、靠女人生活的年轻男子。

examples.zh: 他长得像个小白脸，其实挺能干的。
examples.en: He looks like a pretty boy, but is quite capable.

examples.zh: 她爱上了一个只会花钱的小白脸。
examples.en: She fell in love with a pretty boy who only knew how to spend money.

usage.en: Noun, derogatory and casual; sometimes used jokingly of handsome men.
usage.zh: 名词，口语，贬义，有时也用来戏称英俊男子。

meaning.en: A laboratory mouse; figuratively, a person used as a test subject.
meaning.zh: 实验用的白鼠，比喻被拿来做试验的人。

examples.zh: 新药先在小白鼠身上试验。
examples.en: The new drug is first tested on mice.

examples.zh: 我可不想当他们新系统的小白鼠。
examples.en: I don't want to be the guinea pig for their new system.

usage.en: Noun; the literal lab mouse, or figuratively 当小白鼠 (to be experimented on). Chinese uses mice where English uses guinea pigs.
usage.zh: 名词，既指实验小鼠，也比喻“当小白鼠”被试验。汉语用“小白鼠”，英语说 guinea pig。

meaning.en: An ungrateful person who repays kindness with harm.
meaning.zh: 忘恩负义、恩将仇报的人。

equivalents: one who bites the hand that feeds

examples.zh: 我们帮了他那么多，他却是只白眼狼。
examples.en: We helped him so much, yet he turned out to be an ingrate.

examples.zh: 别养白眼狼，到头来受伤的是自己。
examples.en: Don't nurture an ingrate; you will be the one hurt in the end.

usage.en: Noun, derogatory; wolves are thought to be treacherous, and 白眼 is a contemptuous glare.
usage.zh: 名词，贬义。狼被认为凶狠无情，“白眼”指轻蔑的眼神。

meaning.en: A well-paid, prestigious and stable job.
meaning.zh: 收入高、地位好而且稳定的职业。

examples.zh: 他放弃了金饭碗，出来创业。
examples.en: He gave up his gold-plated job to start a business.

examples.zh: 在银行工作曾经是人人羡慕的金饭碗。
examples.en: Working at a bank used to be a coveted, golden job.

usage.en: Noun, casual; the upgraded form of 铁饭碗 (security alone).
usage.zh: 名词，口语，在“铁饭碗”（稳定）基础上又强调高薪。

meaning.en: A very good idea or suggestion.
meaning.zh: 非常好的主意。

examples.zh: 他提了个金点子，帮公司省了不少钱。
examples.en: He came up with a brilliant idea that saved the company lots of money.

examples.zh: 谁有解决问题的金点子，请大家说一说。
examples.en: If anyone has a bright idea for solving the problem, please share it.

usage.en: Noun, casual; 金点子 is also used for a business idea or a suggestion box.
usage.zh: 名词，口语，也用于企业的好点子、征集建议。

meaning.en: To provoke dangerous people or stir up trouble that is hard to handle.
meaning.zh: 比喻招惹不好惹的人或惹出大麻烦。

examples.zh: 这次调查等于捅了马蜂窝。
examples.en: This investigation amounts to poking a hornet's nest.

examples.zh: 你可别去捅这个马蜂窝。
examples.en: Don't go poking that hornet's nest.

usage.en: Verb-object, casual; 捅了马蜂窝. Related 捅娄子 simply means causing trouble.
usage.zh: 动宾短语，口语，常说“捅了马蜂窝”。与“捅娄子”相比，更强调惹到厉害的人。

natural: go back to an old flame

meaning.en: To return to a former partner, job or choice.
meaning.zh: 回到过去的对象或选择上。

examples.zh: 好马不吃回头草，分手了就别再联系。
examples.en: A good horse doesn't eat the grass it has left behind; once you've split up, don't get in touch again.

examples.zh: 他后来还是吃了回头草，和前女友复合了。
examples.en: He eventually went back to his ex-girlfriend.

usage.en: Verb-object, casual; from the saying 好马不吃回头草 (a good horse never goes back). Often used of couples.
usage.zh: 动宾短语，口语，来自俗语“好马不吃回头草”。常用于感情。

natural: let the team down at a key moment

meaning.en: To fail at a crucial moment.
meaning.zh: 在关键时刻出问题，不能胜任。

examples.zh: 关键时刻他可别掉链子。
examples.en: Let's hope he won't drop the ball at the crunch.

examples.zh: 这场比赛，主力球员接连掉链子。
examples.en: In this match the key players flopped one after another.

usage.en: Verb-object, casual; from a bicycle chain slipping off. 链子 is neutral-toned.
usage.zh: 动宾短语，口语。来自自行车链条脱落。

meaning.en: To act on the very edge of what rules allow, or just over it.
meaning.zh: 在规定的边缘做事，钻空子。

examples.zh: 他们的广告在法律边缘打擦边球。
examples.en: Their advert skirts the edge of the law.

examples.zh: 这种做法就是擦边球，随时可能违规。
examples.en: This approach is a borderline move and might break the rules at any time.

usage.en: Verb-object, casual; from table tennis, where a ball grazing the edge of the table is still in play. Also shortened to 擦边球.
usage.zh: 动宾短语，口语。来自乒乓球，擦到台边的球仍然有效。也可简称“擦边球”。

meaning.en: To deflect questions or responsibilities in a vague, evasive way.
meaning.zh: 比喻推托、敷衍，不正面回答。

examples.zh: 问他什么时候发工资，他只会打太极。
examples.en: Ask him when pay is due and he just dodges.

examples.zh: 领导在会上跟大家打太极，没给明确答复。
examples.en: The boss fenced with us at the meeting and gave no clear answer.

usage.en: Verb-object, casual; derogatory in this sense. Borrowed from tai chi, which uses soft, deflecting moves.
usage.zh: 动宾短语，口语，此义含贬义。借太极拳以柔化刚、顺势化解的特点。

meaning.en: The headquarters or main base of a group or activity.
meaning.zh: 指某一组织或活动的中心地点。

examples.zh: 登山队在山脚下设了大本营。
examples.en: The climbing team set up a base camp at the foot of the mountain.

examples.zh: 这里是我们创业的大本营。
examples.en: This is the base of our start-up.

usage.en: Noun; originally a military term for the main camp, now broader.
usage.zh: 名词，原指军队的主要营地，现在用法更广。

natural: grit one's teeth and go ahead

meaning.en: To go ahead with something unpleasant despite reluctance.
meaning.zh: 明知困难或不愿意，仍勉强去做。

examples.zh: 他硬着头皮上了台，腿还在发抖。
examples.en: He steeled himself and went on stage, his legs still shaking.

examples.zh: 明知道会挨骂，我也只好硬着头皮去。
examples.en: Knowing I'd be told off, I had to go anyway.

usage.en: Adverbial phrase, casual; precedes a verb. The scalp is toughened for a blow.
usage.zh: 状语性短语，口语，用在动词前。头皮变硬，仿佛要承受打击。

meaning.en: A smooth transition that avoids a sharp fall, as in the economy.
meaning.zh: 比喻平稳过渡，避免大起大落，多用于经济。

examples.zh: 专家希望经济能够实现软着陆。
examples.en: Experts hope the economy will achieve a soft landing.

examples.zh: 房地产市场需要软着陆，而不是崩盘。
examples.en: The property market needs a soft landing, not a crash.

usage.en: Noun or verb phrase; originally a spaceflight term for a gentle touchdown. Common in economics and news.
usage.zh: 名词或动词性短语，原是航天术语，指缓慢着陆。常见于经济新闻。

meaning.en: A bold, large-scale piece of work or the person who produces it.
meaning.zh: 规模大的举措，或气魄大、有才能的人。

examples.zh: 这座新体育馆是城市建设的大手笔。
examples.en: This new stadium is a bold stroke in the city's development.

examples.zh: 他出手就是大手笔，一下子捐了一千万。
examples.en: He thinks big; he donated ten million in one go.

usage.en: Noun, casual; originally a great writer or calligrapher, and then bold, generous action.
usage.zh: 名词，口语，原指文章或书法大家，后指气魄大的举动。

meaning.en: To meet strength with strength in a direct clash.
meaning.zh: 以强硬态度正面交锋；也指实打实，不玩虚的。

examples.zh: 两个老板硬碰硬，谁也不肯让步。
examples.en: The two bosses clashed head-on and neither would give way.

examples.zh: 这是一场硬碰硬的比赛，没有任何取巧。
examples.en: This is a hard, straight match with no shortcuts.

usage.en: Phrase, casual; can be neutral or negative about unwise confrontation. In 硬碰硬 the second 硬 is the opponent.
usage.zh: 短语，口语，可中性也可含贬义。也指不取巧，实打实地干。

meaning.en: A person of unyielding spirit; also a tough job or opponent.
meaning.zh: 指意志坚强、不屈服的人，也指难啃的任务或难对付的对手。

examples.zh: 他是条硬骨头，怎么拷问也不开口。
examples.en: He's a tough nut who wouldn't talk however he was pressed.

examples.zh: 这个项目是块硬骨头，得集中力量啃。
examples.en: This project is a hard nut to crack, so we need to concentrate our strength.

usage.en: Noun; positive for a person, neutral for a task (啃硬骨头).
usage.zh: 名词，指人时褒义，指任务时中性，常说“啃硬骨头”。

meaning.en: A rough, uneducated person; often self-deprecating.
meaning.zh: 没有文化、言行粗鲁的人，也常用于自谦。

examples.zh: 我是个大老粗，说话不好听，您别见怪。
examples.en: I'm just a rough fellow and don't speak nicely, so please excuse me.

examples.zh: 别看他是大老粗，心可细了。
examples.en: He may be a coarse man, but he's very thoughtful.

usage.en: Noun, casual; frequently self-deprecating (我是个大老粗).
usage.zh: 名词，口语，常用于自谦，如“我是个大老粗”。

meaning.en: A person or thing used as a means to advance, often at others' expense.
meaning.zh: 比喻借以向上爬的人或事物。

examples.zh: 这份工作只是他职业发展的垫脚石。
examples.en: This job is just a stepping stone in his career.

examples.zh: 他把同事当作升职的垫脚石。
examples.en: He treated his colleagues as stepping stones to promotion.

usage.en: Noun; neutral for a means of progress, negative if people are used. Opposite of 绊脚石.
usage.zh: 名词，指发展的途径时中性，指利用人时含贬义。与“绊脚石”相对。

meaning.en: To be well received and able to get by in a given circle or situation.
meaning.zh: 受欢迎，到哪里都能行得通。

examples.zh: 他人缘好，在哪儿都吃得开。
examples.en: He's popular and gets along anywhere.

examples.zh: 这种手艺现在还吃得开吗？
examples.en: Is this skill still in demand nowadays?

usage.en: Complement structure; negative 吃不开. Describes a person or a skill.
usage.zh: 述补结构，否定式是“吃不开”。可说人，也可说技能。

meaning.en: To offer ideas or suggestions.
meaning.zh: 出主意，提建议。

examples.zh: 大家一起出点子，想想怎么办。
examples.en: Let's all come up with ideas on what to do.

examples.zh: 他不干活，光会出点子。
examples.en: He doesn't do the work; he only offers ideas.

usage.en: Verb-object, casual; 点子 is an idea. Often paired with 想办法.
usage.zh: 动宾短语，口语，“点子”指主意，常与“想办法”并用。

meaning.en: A very close friend, usually male, who can be relied on.
meaning.zh: 关系非常好、靠得住的朋友，多指男性。

examples.zh: 他是我从小一起长大的铁哥们。
examples.en: He's my best buddy since childhood.

examples.zh: 遇到难事，铁哥们总会帮忙。
examples.en: In hard times, your closest buddies will help.

usage.en: Noun, casual, mainly about men; also 铁哥们儿, 铁姐们 for women.
usage.zh: 名词，口语，多指男性，也说“铁哥们儿”，女性可说“铁姐们”。

meaning.en: To sew a patch on clothes; or to apply a software patch or a quick fix.
meaning.zh: 在衣服上缝补，也指给软件安装补丁，或做临时修补。

examples.zh: 奶奶给我的裤子打了个补丁。
examples.en: Grandma sewed a patch on my trousers.

examples.zh: 软件有漏洞，要尽快打补丁。
examples.en: The software has a vulnerability, so we need to patch it quickly.

usage.en: Verb-object; both literal and figurative (to apply a patch to software or policy). 补丁 is read bǔ ding.
usage.zh: 动宾短语，本义和比喻义都常用，如给软件、政策“打补丁”。

meaning.en: To abandon politeness and quarrel openly.
meaning.zh: 不顾情面，公开争吵或翻脸。

examples.zh: 为了钱，他们兄弟俩扯破了脸。
examples.en: The two brothers had an open falling-out over money.

examples.zh: 事情没必要闹到扯破脸的地步。
examples.en: There's no need to go so far as an open row.

usage.en: Verb-object, casual; also 撕破脸. 脸 means face, as in 'saving face'.
usage.zh: 动宾短语，口语，也说“撕破脸”。“脸”指面子。
